headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared file/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can read warehouse data and nullclaw can read/write workspace files, run browsers, use MCP, and ingest webhooks/WS. That creates a plausible bridge where content from dbt outputs or files can be treated as instructions by nullclaw. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so the interaction is possible in default-like workflows.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into nullclaw workspace files or webhook payloads
IF nullclaw parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dbt artifacts into nullclaw
Require provenance tags on all imported files
Route dbt outputs through a read-only staging directory
Turn off MCP endpoints for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while nullclaw handles secrets, workspace files, audit logs, and broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or passes artifacts between them, sensitive warehouse data can flow into nullclaw’s broader exfiltration surface. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary between their file and network paths.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts containing warehouse data are placed in nullclaw's workspace
IF nullclaw forwards workspace files or logs to external services
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs in a separate read-only directory
Block nullclaw access to dbt artifact paths
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict nullclaw egress to approved destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem and network isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call data-warehouse APIs, and nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and use broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or project directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict is dangerous by default in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git working tree
IF dbt-core and nullclaw write artifacts or commit state concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a git lock or serialized commit queue
Make dbt outputs read-only to nullclaw
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived outputs, and nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, browsers, and shell commands. If nullclaw treats dbt output as authoritative, a bad model or malformed artifact can cascade into downstream actions or commits. No verification step is documented between them, so the pair can amplify errors into operational changes.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes dbt-generated artifacts without validation
IF nullclaw uses those artifacts to trigger shell, webhook, or git actions
mitigations: Require human review before acting on dbt outputs
Validate schemas before nullclaw consumes artifacts
Disable auto-commit from dbt-derived files
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while nullclaw handles audit logs, workspace files, and multiple secret classes. If warehouse data includes regulated records, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because nullclaw’s broad egress and logging surfaces are not shown to match dbt’s data-governance constraints. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data from the warehouse is processed through nullclaw logs or workspace files
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the warehouse and nullclaw storage
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from the pair
Minimize logging of warehouse-derived content
Set explicit retention limits on nullclaw artifacts
Review residency for any external egress
requires-engineering: align compliance policies across both systems
